proof:
The work fact actual-mixed-own-depth-envelope-work gives the endpoint exchange and positive-fiber interior of every selected source. The integer midpoint belongs to $S$ by convexity and equal parity, and 4e868f774de77608 gives $\Delta\ge0$. Since $F(Y_m)>0$, its fiber is positive and its mark interior. Apply 1ec728c26c11b368 to the same finite nonempty sampled family, with its raw mixed $d$-volume, to obtain a finite nonvertical depth cap. If $n=0$, use the same dummy base as in the work fact for both accepted theorems. Normalize its continuous normal to length one. All its nonvertical level boundaries are null on the positive fibers.

Whenever an endpoint $Y_e$ has margin $s_e=L(Y_e)\ge0$, the exact difference between the cap mass and the parallel shifted mass is $\mu\{0\le L<s_e\}$. The latter shifted cap contains $Y_e$ and therefore has mass at least $D_e$. If $s_e>0$, the lost portion of the centered own-fiber ball at $Y_e$ has positive volume, so the difference is strict. At $\delta>0$, maximizing at $\lambda_0$ yields
$$
D(Y_m)\le D_0-\lambda_0(\delta/2+\Delta).
$$
If $\lambda_0>0$, the cap cannot contain $Y_0$ even on its boundary, as its mass is strictly less than $D_0$. If $\lambda_0=0$, it cannot contain $Y_0$ at strictly positive margin because the parallel shift just proved would give mass strictly greater than $D_0$. The affine margins at the endpoints are opposite. Thus $Y_1$ has the stated sign in either case. Combining its parallel shift with this inequality and with $P_{\lambda_1}(Y_m)\le P_{\lambda_1}(Y_1)$ gives the two endpoint budgets. If $\lambda_0>0$, $T_H>0$ gives $\Delta<\delta/2$ and $D(Y_m)>D_1$, and the other strict inequalities follow from the displayed bound and $\delta>0$.

If $\delta=0$ then $A=0$. Every cap containing the midpoint contains an endpoint, so $D(Y_m)\ge D_0$. The $\lambda_1$ objective and $\Delta\ge0$ force equality and $\Delta=0$. Neither endpoint can have strictly positive margin in a critical cap by the positive slab argument. Since the margins are opposite, both are zero.

For distinct parameters and $\delta>0$, the two endpoint affine lines cross at $\lambda_*=A/\delta\in[\lambda_0,\lambda_1]$. They have value $D_0+\lambda_*F_0$ there, so $B\ge0$. Combining $D(Y_m)+\lambda_*F(Y_m)\le E(\lambda_*)$ with the shift to $Y_1$ gives $T_H+\lambda_*\Delta\le A/2+B$. The same calculation for an endpoint chosen solely by nonnegative margin gives right side $A/2+B$ at $Y_1$ and $-A/2+B$ at $Y_0$. For the bound on $B$, interpolate the values $E(\lambda_i)=D_i+\lambda_iF_i$. Subtract the line of source zero from the chord. Its residual at $\lambda_0$ is zero, and at $\lambda_1$ is $\delta(\lambda_1-\lambda_*)$. Hence its residual at $\lambda_*$ is exactly the displayed product divided by the parameter interval length. Convexity bounds $E$ by that chord, and the product is at most one quarter of the interval length squared. At equal parameters both endpoint lines are active at their intersection, so $B=0$ and the direct comparison there gives the same budget. The zero-increment convention follows from the previous paragraph.

In the endpoint ball put $t=s-L$ along its continuous normal. The part with $0\le L<s$ corresponds to $0<t\le\min(s,r)$, with the stated cross-section areas. Up to $r/2$ every section radius is at least $\sqrt3 r/2$. For the available radius, any parallel section of the endpoint fiber fits in a $(d-1)$-ball of radius $R$ about a point of the section. The cap through the mark has volume at most that section bound times the distance from the mark to the parallel support plane. Its volume is at least $F_1^d$, so every support distance is at least the displayed radius. The intersection of the supporting halfspaces thus contains the centered ball. In dimension one the section count is at most one and the same reasoning is the endpoint distance. If $\epsilon<c_r r/2$ then the slab lower bound forces $s<r/2$ and $s\le\epsilon/c_r$. Since the margins are opposite, the full coupled normal difference is $2s$. The endpoint is selected at a positive parameter, so the work fact gives $F_1\ge F_*>0$ and a common radius follows using the largest sampled fiber diameter.

Sum the edge bounds $A_j/2+B_j$, with zero gain and zero charge on a repeated source. The $A_j$ telescope and the $B_j$ give the product or mesh bounds in the statement. Root gains are nonnegative, so discarding them and applying finite subadditivity bounds the original slab union. The work identity applies to the first term for the canonical slope choices, including jumps. If one first restricts the sequence to a single parity class, each edge is measured in that subsequence and can skip arbitrarily many full-sequence parameters. This derivation supplies an upper bound for the union of the chosen slabs.

statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Take distinct maximizers $Y_i=(z_i,x_i)$ at $0\le\lambda_0\le\lambda_1$, with $\lambda_1>0$ and the two bases of equal parity. At equal parameters order the sources by nondecreasing own root. Write $F_i=F(Y_i)$, $D_i=D(Y_i)$, $\delta=F_1-F_0$, $A=D_0-D_1$, $Y_m=(Y_0+Y_1)/2$ and $\Delta=F(Y_m)-(F_0+F_1)/2\ge0$. For every nonvertical depth-attaining cap through $Y_m$, write $H=\{L\ge0\}$ with $L(z,x)=a\cdot(z-z_m)+u\cdot(x-x_m)$ and $\lVert u\rVert=1$. Then $L(Y_1)\ge0$, strictly if $\lambda_0>0$ and $\delta>0$. Set $T_H=\mu\{0\le L<L(Y_1)\}$; this is the exact mass removed by shifting the same cap to $Y_1$, and $D(Y_m)\ge D_1+T_H$. When $\delta>0$,
$$
T_H+\lambda_0\Delta\le A-\lambda_0\delta/2,\qquad
T_H+\lambda_1\Delta\le\lambda_1\delta/2.
$$
If in addition $\lambda_0>0$, then $0\le\Delta<\delta/2$, $F_0<F(Y_m)<F_1$ and $D_1<D(Y_m)<D_0$. For distinct parameters put $\lambda_*=A/\delta$ and $B=E(\lambda_*)-D_0-\lambda_*F_0$. Then
$$
T_H+\lambda_*\Delta\le A/2+B,\qquad
0\le B\le
\frac{\delta(\lambda_*-\lambda_0)(\lambda_1-\lambda_*)}{\lambda_1-\lambda_0}
\le(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)\delta/4.
$$
For equal parameters take $\lambda_*=\lambda_1$ and $B=0$. For $\delta=0$ both endpoint margins, $\Delta,T_H,A$ and $B$ are zero and one can take any $\lambda_*\in[\lambda_0,\lambda_1]$.

Write $s=L(Y_1)$ and suppose the endpoint fiber contains a centered ball of radius $r>0$. For $\kappa_j$ the unit $j$-ball volume, $\kappa_0=1$, one has
$$
T_H\ge \kappa_{d-1}\int_0^{\min(s,r)}(r^2-t^2)^{(d-1)/2}\,dt
\ge c_r\min(s,r/2),\qquad c_r=\kappa_{d-1}(\sqrt3 r/2)^{d-1}.
$$
For $d=1$ the integral expression is $\min(s,r)$. An available radius is $r=F_1^d/(\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1})$ for $R=\operatorname{diam}C_{z_1}$. If $T_H\le\epsilon<c_r r/2$, then $|a\cdot(z_1-z_0)+u\cdot(x_1-x_0)|\le2\epsilon/c_r$. One can choose a common positive radius from the body's maximum fiber diameter and the positive slope floor $F_*$.

For a finite chain of selected sources at nondecreasing positive parameters $\lambda_j$, order equal-parameter sources by their own roots and assume successive bases have equal parity. Let $(T_j,\Delta_j,\lambda_{*,j})$ denote these quantities for each edge, and set $\eta=\max_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)$. Then
$$
\sum_j(T_j+\lambda_{*,j}\Delta_j)\le
\frac{D_0-D_N}{2}+\frac14\sum_j(\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j)(F_{j+1}-F_j)
\le \frac{D_0-D_N}{2}+\frac{\eta(F_N-F_0)}4 .
$$
The same upper budget bounds the original measure of the union of the slabs. Along canonical envelope selections the first term is half of the corresponding work integral. Parity subsequences use the successive gaps within each subsequence.
title: Actual midpoint slabs are bounded by envelope gaps and depth drops
